subject: ELA
title: ELA 2
description: A year of second-grade English Language Arts built around real books: Frog and Toad, Aesop's fables, Beatrix Potter, Robert Louis Stevenson's poems, Cinderella tales from many cultures, biographies, science read-alouds, and Winnie-the-Pooh. Every week blends daily phonics and word study (vowel teams, r-controlled vowels, prefixes and suffixes), fluency practice, grammar, a writing project (narrative, informative, opinion, research), and speaking and listening. Day 5 reviews the week with a spelling check, fluency read, and short comprehension or writing assessment.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy; 2014 California ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.2.1: Ask and answer who, what, where, when, why, and how questions to show understanding of key details in a story.
standards.RL.2.2: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
standards.RL.2.3: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
standards.RL.2.4: Describe how words and phrases (regular beats, alliteration, rhymes, repeated lines) supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
standards.RL.2.5: Describe the overall structure of a story, including how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
standards.RL.2.6: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including speaking in a different voice for each character when reading aloud.
standards.RL.2.7: Use information from illustrations and words in a print or digital text to show understanding of characters, setting, or plot.
standards.RL.2.9: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story (e.g., Cinderella stories) by different authors or from different cultures.
standards.RL.2.10: Read and comprehend literature, including stories and poetry, in the grades 2–3 text complexity band.
standards.RI.2.1: Ask and answer who, what, where, when, why, and how questions about key details in an informational text.
standards.RI.2.2: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text and the focus of specific paragraphs within it.
standards.RI.2.3: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas, or steps in technical procedures.
standards.RI.2.4: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a grade 2 topic or subject-area text.
standards.RI.2.5: Know and use text features (captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, menus, icons) to locate key facts efficiently.
standards.RI.2.6: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
standards.RI.2.7: Explain how specific images (e.g., a diagram showing how a machine works) contribute to and clarify a text.
standards.RI.2.8: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
standards.RI.2.9: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
standards.RI.2.10: Read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 2–3 band.
standards.RF.2.3a: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.
standards.RF.2.3b: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
standards.RF.2.3c: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
standards.RF.2.3d: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
standards.RF.2.3e: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
standards.RF.2.3f: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
standards.RF.2.4: Read on-level text with sufficient accuracy and fluency (purpose, rate, expression), using context to self-correct.
standards.W.2.1: Write opinion pieces that introduce the topic, state an opinion, supply reasons using linking words, and provide a concluding statement.
standards.W.2.2: Write informative/explanatory texts that introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement.
standards.W.2.3: Write narratives that recount a well-elaborated event or short sequence of events with details, temporal words, and a sense of closure.
standards.W.2.5: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing by revising and editing.
standards.W.2.6: With guidance and support, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.
standards.W.2.7: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., read books on a single topic to produce a report).
standards.W.2.8: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
standards.SL.2.1: Participate in collaborative conversations about grade 2 topics and texts, following agreed-upon rules and building on others' talk.
standards.SL.2.2: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
standards.SL.2.3: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says to clarify comprehension or gather more information.
standards.SL.2.4: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.
standards.SL.2.5: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to stories or recounts to clarify ideas.
standards.SL.2.6: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.L.2.1a: Use collective nouns (e.g., group, herd, flock).
standards.L.2.1b: Form and use frequently occurring irregular plural nouns (e.g., feet, children, teeth, mice, fish).
standards.L.2.1d: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs (e.g., sat, hid, told).
standards.L.2.1e: Use adjectives and adverbs, and choose between them depending on what is to be modified.
standards.L.2.1f: Produce, expand, and rearrange complete simple and compound sentences.
standards.L.2.2: Use capitalization (holidays, product and geographic names), commas in letters, apostrophes for contractions and possessives, learned spelling patterns, and reference materials when writing.
standards.L.2.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions; compare formal and informal uses of English.
standards.L.2.4: Determine or clarify unknown words using sentence context, prefixes, root words, compound-word parts, and glossaries or dictionaries.
standards.L.2.5: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances (real-life connections; shades of meaning among related verbs and adjectives).
standards.L.2.6: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading, and being read to, including adjectives and adverbs to describe.

resources.name: Project Gutenberg
resources.note: Free public-domain texts used this year: Aesop's Fables, The Tale of Peter Rabbit, The Velveteen Rabbit, A Child's Garden of Verses, The Blue Fairy Book (Cinderella), Winnie-the-Pooh.

resources.name: ReadWorks
resources.note: Free leveled grade 2 fiction and nonfiction passages with question sets (animals, biographies, Earth science).

resources.name: Storyline Online
resources.note: Free videos of actors reading picture books aloud; good for listening comprehension days.

resources.name: Khan Academy – 2nd grade reading & vocabulary
resources.note: Free reading passages and vocabulary practice aligned to grade 2.

resources.name: PBS LearningMedia
resources.note: Free videos and games (Between the Lions, WordGirl, Martha Speaks) for phonics and vocabulary.

units.title: Friends and Feelings: Story Elements
units.big_idea: Good readers notice characters, settings, and events, and good writers tell true stories with details.

units.title: Fables and Folktales
units.big_idea: Stories from many cultures teach lessons about how to live.

units.title: Amazing Animals: Reading for Information
units.big_idea: Informational texts use features like headings, glossaries, and diagrams to teach facts.

units.title: Characters Who Change
units.big_idea: Characters respond to big events, and stories have beginnings that introduce and endings that conclude.

units.title: Poetry and Word Play
units.big_idea: Poets use rhythm, rhyme, repetition, and carefully chosen words to create meaning and feeling.

units.title: Cinderella Around the World and Point of View
units.big_idea: The same story changes when told by different cultures or from a different character's point of view.

units.title: People Who Make a Difference: Biographies
units.big_idea: Biographies connect the events of a real person's life and show how one person can change the world.

units.title: Our Changing Earth: Comparing Texts
units.big_idea: Authors give reasons to support their points, and two texts on one topic can teach different things.

units.title: Chapter Book Club and Year-End Celebration
units.big_idea: Readers follow characters across chapters and share opinions about books they love.

weeks.topic: Reading routines with Frog and Toad
objectives: Ask and answer who/what/where questions about a story
Read short-a and short-i words
Write complete sentences with capitals and end marks
materials: Frog and Toad Are Friends (Arnold Lobel)

days.title: Meet Frog and Toad
days.work: Read aloud 'Spring' from Frog and Toad Are Friends, then answer who/what/where questions orally and draw the setting. Start a reading log and practice the book-talk rule 'listen, then add on.'

days.title: Short a and short i
days.work: Phonics: blend and read short-a/short-i words (cap, cab, pin, fit), then sort 12 word cards into two columns. Reread 'Spring' to a parent for fluency and write 2 sentences telling what Frog wanted.

days.title: What makes a sentence
days.work: Grammar: learn that a sentence tells a whole idea and starts with a capital and ends with a period, question mark, or exclamation point; fix 6 scrambled sentences. Read 'The Story' and answer 3 why/how questions.

days.title: Character talk
days.work: Partner talk: describe Toad using two words and evidence from the pictures in 'The Story'. Write 3 complete sentences about a friend you like to be with.

days.title: Week 1 review
days.work: Spelling check of 10 short-a/short-i words, a one-minute timed read of a Frog and Toad page, and a 3-question oral comprehension check. Record books read in the reading log.

weeks.assessment: Spelling check (10 words), oral who/what/where answers, and correctly punctuated sentences in journal.

weeks.topic: How characters respond to problems
objectives: Describe how a character responds to a major event
Read short-o, short-u and short-e words
Identify common nouns

days.title: A Lost Button
days.work: Read 'A Lost Button' and list on sticky notes each button Frog and Toad find; discuss how Toad feels as each wrong button is found. Phonics: read short-o words (hop, lot, pond).

days.title: Problem and solution
days.work: Fill in a problem/solution chart for 'A Lost Button' and tell how Toad responds at the end (he sews buttons on the jacket). Phonics: short-u and short-e word sort (bug, bed, cup, net).

days.title: Nouns are naming words
days.work: Grammar: circle nouns (people, places, things) in 8 sentences from the story, then list 10 nouns you can see at home. Read 'A Swim' with expression.

days.title: Small moment ideas
days.work: Writing: brainstorm 3 'small moments' from your own summer and pick one; sketch it in 3 boxes (beginning, middle, end). Tell the story aloud to a listener using details.

days.title: Week 2 review
days.work: Spelling check of 10 short-o/u/e words, retell 'A Lost Button' in order using first/next/last, and write one sentence about how Toad changed. Add titles to reading log.

weeks.assessment: Problem/solution chart, spelling check, and oral retell checked for correct sequence.

weeks.topic: Digraphs and drafting a personal narrative
objectives: Read words with sh, ch, th, wh, ck
Use collective nouns
Draft a personal narrative with temporal words

days.title: The List
days.work: Read 'A List' from Frog and Toad Together and make your own to-do list for the day. Phonics: read and write sh/ch/th words (ship, chop, thin, wish, much, bath).

days.title: Cookies and willpower
days.work: Read 'Cookies' and answer why Frog and Toad cannot stop eating cookies and how they try to solve it. Phonics: wh and ck words (when, whip, duck, sock) in a word ladder.

days.title: Collective nouns
days.work: Grammar: match collective nouns to groups (a flock of birds, a herd of cows, a team of players, a class of students) and write 4 sentences using them. Read 'The Garden' aloud with a partner.

days.title: Draft my story
days.work: Writing: draft the small moment chosen last week using temporal words (first, next, then, after that, finally) to show the order. Include what you saw, heard, and felt.

days.title: Week 3 review
days.work: Spelling check of 10 digraph words, collective-noun matching quiz, and read the narrative draft aloud to a family member who asks one question about it.

weeks.assessment: Spelling check, collective-noun quiz (8 items), and narrative draft with at least 3 temporal words.

weeks.topic: Henry and Mudge; revising and sharing stories
objectives: Read words with consonant blends
Revise a narrative by adding details and feelings
Tell a story audibly in complete sentences
materials: Henry and Mudge: The First Book (Cynthia Rylant)

days.title: Henry and Mudge
days.work: Read Henry and Mudge: The First Book, chapters 1–2, and describe how Henry feels before and after he gets Mudge. Phonics: read initial blends (bl, cr, st, fl) in 15 words.

days.title: Henry gets lost
days.work: Read chapter 3 and discuss how Henry and Mudge each respond when Mudge gets lost. Phonics: final blends (-nd, -st, -mp) word building with letter tiles.

days.title: Revise with details
days.work: Writing: reread the narrative draft and add 2 details and a feeling sentence using a colored pencil ('My heart was pounding'). Edit for capitals and end marks with a checklist.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Writing: copy the revised narrative neatly, add an illustration for each part, and give it a title. Practice reading it aloud at a steady pace with expression.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Author's chair: read the published narrative aloud to the family and answer listeners' questions. Complete a unit check: blends/digraph spelling (12 words) and a short story-element quiz on a new Frog and Toad story.

weeks.assessment: Published personal narrative scored with a simple rubric (sequence, details, closing, conventions) plus unit spelling and story-element quiz.

weeks.topic: Aesop's fables: the lesson of the story
objectives: Recount a fable in order
Determine a fable's moral
Read CVCe long-vowel words

days.title: The Lion and the Mouse
days.work: Listen to 'The Lion and the Mouse' from Aesop's Fables and retell it with 4 sequence cards. Discuss the moral: little friends can be great friends.

days.title: Magic e
days.work: Phonics: change CVC to CVCe words (cap/cape, kit/kite, hop/hope, cub/cube) and read 20 long-vowel words. Write 3 sentences using CVCe words.

days.title: Tortoise and the Hare
days.work: Read 'The Tortoise and the Hare' and compare how each character responds to the race. Write the moral in your own words: 'Slow and steady wins the race' means…

days.title: Proper nouns
days.work: Grammar: capitalize names of people, pets, and places; fix 8 sentences with missing capitals. Retell a fable to a family member using first, next, then, last.

days.title: Week 5 review
days.work: Spelling check of 10 CVCe words, match 4 fables to their morals, and read a new fable ('The Fox and the Grapes') independently and write its lesson in one sentence.

weeks.assessment: Fable-moral matching, written moral for a new fable, and CVCe spelling check.

weeks.topic: Fables continued: vowel teams ai/ay and ee/ea
objectives: Read words with vowel teams ai, ay, ee, ea
Use irregular plural nouns
Explain how a fable's lesson connects to life

days.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
days.work: Read 'The Ant and the Grasshopper' and chart what each character does in summer and in winter. Phonics: ai/ay words (rain, train, play, day).

days.title: The Crow and the Pitcher
days.work: Read 'The Crow and the Pitcher' and test the idea at home by dropping pebbles into a cup of water. Phonics: ee/ea words (tree, green, beach, read).

days.title: Irregular plurals
days.work: Grammar: learn plurals that change (foot/feet, child/children, tooth/teeth, mouse/mice, fish/fish) and complete 10 fill-in sentences. Read a fable aloud using complete sentences to answer 'What is the lesson?'

days.title: Fable connection
days.work: Write 3–4 sentences about a time in your life when one of this week's morals came true. Draw a picture to go with it.

days.title: Week 6 review
days.work: Spelling check of 12 vowel-team words, an irregular-plurals quiz, and a fluency read of 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf' with an oral moral check.

weeks.assessment: Spelling check, 10-item irregular plural quiz, and written fable-to-life connection.

weeks.topic: Folktales from many cultures and character voices
objectives: Recount folktales and identify their central message
Read oa/ow/oe and igh/ie/y long-vowel spellings
Read with a different voice for each character
materials: Stone Soup (Marcia Brown or Jon J Muth)

days.title: The Little Red Hen
days.work: Read The Little Red Hen and discuss why the hen would not share the bread; decide if that was fair. Phonics: oa/ow/oe words (boat, snow, toe).

days.title: Stone Soup
days.work: Read Stone Soup and compare its lesson about sharing with The Little Red Hen. Phonics: igh/ie/y words (night, pie, fly) in a sentence-building game.

days.title: Voices for characters
days.work: Practice reading Little Red Hen dialogue using a different voice for the hen, dog, cat, and duck. Make paper-bag puppets of each character.

days.title: Retell in writing
days.work: Write a 5-sentence retelling of Stone Soup with a beginning, middle, and end and the lesson in the last sentence. Underline time-order words.

days.title: Week 7 review
days.work: Perform The Little Red Hen as a puppet show using character voices. Spelling check of 12 long-o and long-i words and a written central-message question.

weeks.assessment: Puppet-show performance (voice and fluency), spelling check, and written central message.

weeks.topic: Anansi tales and writing an original fable
objectives: Determine the lesson of a trickster tale
Plan, draft, and edit an original fable
Perform reader's theater
materials: Anansi and the Moss-Covered Rock (Eric A. Kimmel)

days.title: Anansi the trickster
days.work: Read Anansi and the Moss-Covered Rock (West African folktale) and explain how Little Bush Deer teaches Anansi a lesson. Note how the beginning introduces Anansi's trick and the ending wraps it up.

days.title: Plan a fable
days.work: Writing: choose two animal characters with opposite traits and a lesson; plan beginning, problem, and ending on a fable organizer. Phonics review: vowel-team word hunt in the Anansi book.

days.title: Draft the fable
days.work: Draft the original fable with dialogue and a moral as the last line. Read it to a listener and ask 'Was my lesson clear?'

days.title: Edit and publish
days.work: Edit with a checklist (capitals, end marks, spelling of vowel-team words) and publish with illustrations. Rehearse a reader's theater script of 'The Lion and the Mouse.'

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Perform the reader's theater and read your fable aloud. Unit test: read a new folktale, write its moral, sequence 4 events, and spell 12 long-vowel words.

weeks.assessment: Original fable (rubric: characters, problem, moral, conventions) and unit test on a cold-read folktale.

weeks.topic: Nonfiction text features
objectives: Use headings, bold words, captions, and glossaries to find facts
Read ar and or words
Distinguish nouns from verbs
materials: National Geographic Readers: Frogs! (Elizabeth Carney) or any National Geographic Kids reader

days.title: Fiction or nonfiction
days.work: Sort 10 library books into fiction and nonfiction and explain the clues. Take a text-feature tour of Frogs! and flag a heading, caption, bold word, and glossary.

days.title: Feature scavenger hunt
days.work: Use the table of contents and index to answer 5 questions from Frogs! (e.g., 'What page tells what frogs eat?'). Phonics: ar words (car, farm, star).

days.title: Glossary words
days.work: Look up 5 bold words in the glossary and draw a picture for each. Phonics: or words (corn, storm, horse) in a word sort.

days.title: Nouns and verbs
days.work: Grammar: sort words from Frogs! into nouns and verbs (frog, leap, pond, swim). Write 4 fact sentences, each with a noun and a verb.

days.title: Week 9 review
days.work: Use text features to answer 6 questions from a new ReadWorks animal passage. Spelling check of 10 ar/or words.

weeks.assessment: Text-feature scavenger hunt (6 questions on a new text) and spelling check.

weeks.topic: Life cycles: connecting steps in a process
objectives: Describe the connection between stages of a life cycle
Read er, ir, ur words
Take notes from a source

days.title: Monarch life cycle
days.work: Read Monarch Butterfly by Gail Gibbons and list the 4 stages (egg, larva, pupa, adult). Phonics: er/ir/ur words (her, bird, turn) — same sound, different spellings.

days.title: Connecting steps
days.work: Make a paper-plate life-cycle wheel and explain how each stage leads to the next using because and then. Learn the subject words larva and chrysalis from context.

days.title: Taking notes
days.work: Learn to take notes in words, not sentences; record 6 facts about monarchs on a note sheet. Phonics: er/ir/ur spelling sort.

days.title: Migration question
days.work: Read the migration section and answer in writing 'Why do monarchs fly to California and Mexico?' using notes. Share answers and ask a partner a clarifying question.

days.title: Week 10 review
days.work: Sequence the life cycle in a labeled drawing, spell 10 r-controlled words, and answer 4 questions on a ReadWorks butterfly passage.

weeks.assessment: Labeled life-cycle drawing, written migration answer from notes, and spelling check.

weeks.topic: Main topic, paragraphs, and diagrams
objectives: Identify the main topic and paragraph focus
Explain how a diagram clarifies a text
Draft an informative paragraph

days.title: Main topic
days.work: Read From Tadpole to Frog and name the main topic; reread 3 paragraphs and tell what each one is mostly about. Phonics: y as long e and long i (happy, sky).

days.title: Diagrams help
days.work: Study the diagram of the frog life cycle and explain what it shows that the words do not. Draw your own labeled diagram of a tadpole.

days.title: Choose an animal
days.work: Choose an animal for an 'All About' report, read 2 library books on it, and take notes in 3 boxes: body, home, food.

days.title: Topic sentences
days.work: Learn that an informative paragraph starts with a topic sentence; draft paragraph 1 (body) with a topic sentence and 3 facts. Phonics: y word sort.

days.title: Week 11 review
days.work: Read a new 3-paragraph passage and write the main topic and the focus of each paragraph. Spelling check of y-as-vowel words.

weeks.assessment: Main-topic and paragraph-focus organizer on a cold read; first report paragraph.

weeks.topic: Author's purpose and publishing an animal report
objectives: Identify an author's main purpose
Write and publish an informative report with a diagram
Present facts and answer questions

days.title: Why did the author write it
days.work: Compare the purpose of Frogs! (teach facts) to a Frog and Toad story (entertain); decide what question Monarch Butterfly answers. Finish report paragraph 2 (home).

days.title: Finish the draft
days.work: Write paragraph 3 (food) and a concluding sentence. Add a labeled diagram and a glossary of 3 words to the report.

days.title: Revise and edit
days.work: Read the report aloud and fix anything that does not make sense; check spelling of r-controlled and vowel-team words. Make a final copy on cardstock.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the animal report to family or a video call, speaking clearly and answering 2 questions from listeners. Listeners ask one question to gather more information.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Cold read of a nonfiction passage with questions on text features, main topic, and author's purpose. Spelling test of 15 r-controlled and y words.

weeks.assessment: Published 'All About' report (rubric: topic sentence, facts, diagram, conclusion) and unit reading test.

weeks.topic: Peter Rabbit: story structure and irregular past tense
objectives: Describe how the beginning introduces and the ending concludes a story
Use irregular past-tense verbs
Read oi/oy words
materials: The Tale of Peter Rabbit (Beatrix Potter, public domain)

days.title: Meet Peter
days.work: Read The Tale of Peter Rabbit and fill a story map; discuss what the beginning tells us (Mother's warning). Phonics: oi/oy words (coin, boy, soil, toy).

days.title: Peter responds
days.work: Reread and describe how Peter responds to Mr. McGregor chasing him, using the illustrations as evidence. Write 3 sentences about his feelings.

days.title: Past tense irregular verbs
days.work: Grammar: learn ran, went, ate, hid, sat, told, found from the story and complete 10 sentences. Phonics: oi/oy spelling sort.

days.title: How it ends
days.work: Discuss how the ending (chamomile tea vs. blackberries) concludes the story and teaches a lesson. Rewrite the ending in 4 sentences as if Peter had listened.

days.title: Week 13 review
days.work: Spelling check of 10 oi/oy words, irregular past-tense quiz, and a story-map check on 'The Tale of Benjamin Bunny' read aloud.

weeks.assessment: Story map for a new Potter tale, irregular past-tense quiz, spelling check.

weeks.topic: The Velveteen Rabbit and planning a fiction story
objectives: Track how a character changes across a longer story
Read oo, au, aw words
Plan a fictional narrative
materials: The Velveteen Rabbit (Margery Williams, public domain)

days.title: Velveteen Rabbit part 1
days.work: Read the first half of The Velveteen Rabbit aloud and discuss what the Skin Horse means by 'Real.' Phonics: oo words in two sounds (moon, book).

days.title: Velveteen Rabbit part 2
days.work: Finish the story and chart how the Rabbit changes from beginning to end. Phonics: au/aw words (sauce, draw, paw).

days.title: Past tense in writing
days.work: Write 5 sentences retelling the Rabbit's adventures using irregular past-tense verbs (was, became, went, grew, saw). Read the sentences to check they sound right.

days.title: Plan my story
days.work: Plan an original fiction story with a toy or animal character on a story-mountain organizer: beginning, problem, events, solution, ending.

days.title: Week 14 review
days.work: Answer who/what/why questions about the Velveteen Rabbit in writing, spelling check of 12 oo/au/aw words, and share the story plan.

weeks.assessment: Written comprehension answers, spelling check, completed story plan.

weeks.topic: Feelings, shades of meaning, adjectives and adverbs
objectives: Describe characters' feelings with precise words
Use adjectives and adverbs
Draft a fictional narrative

days.title: Chrysanthemum
days.work: Read Chrysanthemum and use the pictures to show how her feelings change each day of school. Discuss why words can hurt or help.

days.title: Shades of meaning
days.work: Order feeling words on paint-chip strips (glad, happy, thrilled; sad, upset, miserable) and verbs (toss, throw, hurl). Use 3 in sentences about Chrysanthemum.

days.title: Adjectives and adverbs
days.work: Grammar: adjectives describe nouns (a long name) and adverbs describe verbs (she walked slowly); sort 12 words and write 4 sentences. Phonics: soft c and g (city, gem, face, page).

days.title: Draft my story
days.work: Draft the fiction story from the plan, using at least 3 adjectives, 2 adverbs, and dialogue. Write a beginning that introduces the character and setting.

days.title: Week 15 review
days.work: Spelling check of soft c/g words, adjective-or-adverb quiz, and reread the draft aloud to find one place to add a feeling word.

weeks.assessment: Adjective/adverb quiz, spelling check, story draft checked for beginning and descriptive words.

weeks.topic: Ira Sleeps Over; revising and publishing fiction
objectives: Revise and edit a narrative with peer and adult feedback
Read irregular high-frequency words
Read aloud with fluency

days.title: Ira's choice
days.work: Read Ira Sleeps Over and discuss how Ira responds to his sister's teasing and how he decides about his teddy bear. Practice irregular words (could, would, should, through, though).

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Read your story draft to a family member who gives one 'star' (something good) and one 'wish' (something to improve). Revise based on the wish.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit with a checklist: capitals, end marks, quotation marks for dialogue, and spelling of this unit's patterns. Fix past-tense verbs.

days.title: Publish the book
days.work: Publish the story as a stapled book with a cover, title page, and illustrations. Practice reading it aloud smoothly three times.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Fluency check: one-minute read of an on-level passage (goal about 70–90 words correct) with expression. Unit test on a new story: character response, beginning/ending, and adjective/adverb use.

weeks.assessment: Published fiction book (narrative rubric), fluency WCPM record, and unit test.

weeks.topic: Poems with rhythm and rhyme
objectives: Describe how rhyme and beat supply rhythm
Read compound words
Recite a poem with expression
materials: A Child's Garden of Verses (Robert Louis Stevenson, public domain)
drum or pot to tap beat

days.title: My Shadow
days.work: Read Stevenson's 'My Shadow' aloud and tap the beat; highlight rhyming pairs at line ends. Discuss what the shadow does.

days.title: The Swing
days.work: Read 'The Swing' and act out the rhythm while swinging arms; discuss how the beat feels like swinging. Phonics: compound words (sunshine, rainbow, playground) — split and define.

days.title: Compound word meaning
days.work: Use the two smaller words to figure out meanings of 10 compound words (birdhouse, bookshelf, notebook). Write a rhyming couplet using one.

days.title: Memorize
days.work: Memorize the first stanza of 'My Shadow' and practice reciting with expression and clear volume. Read 'Rain' and 'Where Go the Boats?' for fun.

days.title: Week 17 review
days.work: Recite the stanza, find rhymes and beats in a new poem, and take a spelling check of 10 compound words.

weeks.assessment: Poem recitation (memory, expression, volume), rhyme/beat identification on a new poem, spelling check.

weeks.topic: Alliteration, repetition, and two-syllable words
objectives: Identify alliteration and repeated lines
Decode two-syllable words with long vowels
Write a list poem
materials: Where the Sidewalk Ends (Shel Silverstein) or a library poetry anthology

days.title: Alliteration
days.work: Read tongue twisters ('Peter Piper') and Mother Goose rhymes; underline repeated beginning sounds. Write your own alliterative sentence about your name.

days.title: Repeated lines
days.work: Read Christina Rossetti's 'Who Has Seen the Wind?' and talk about how the repeated question gives the poem its rhythm and meaning.

days.title: Two-syllable words
days.work: Phonics: split two-syllable words with long vowels (re-peat, pa-per, rain-coat, ex-plain) and read 20 words. Clap syllables in poem lines.

days.title: List poem
days.work: Write a list poem about 'Things I Hear at Night' using describing words and a repeated line. Illustrate it.

days.title: Week 18 mid-year check
days.work: Mid-year assessment: phonics inventory (vowel teams, r-controlled, two-syllable words), fluency read, and a poem comprehension question about rhythm and repetition.

weeks.assessment: Mid-year phonics inventory and fluency record; list poem.

weeks.topic: Sensory poems and compound sentences
objectives: Use adjectives and adverbs in poems
Form compound sentences with and, but, or, so
Read words with -ed and -ing endings

days.title: Five senses poem
days.work: Go outside and list what you see, hear, smell, feel, and taste; turn the list into a 5-line senses poem. Read Stevenson's 'Rain' and 'Windy Nights' for models.

days.title: Compound sentences
days.work: Grammar: join two short sentences with and, but, or, so and a comma ('The wind blew, and the leaves fell.'); combine 8 pairs. Phonics: doubling before -ing (run/running).

days.title: Endings -ed
days.work: Phonics: read -ed words with three sounds (jumped, played, wanted) and sort them. Use 3 in compound sentences.

days.title: Word choice
days.work: Revise yesterday's senses poem by swapping 3 plain words for stronger words (said → whispered, big → enormous). Read it aloud to compare versions.

days.title: Week 19 review
days.work: Spelling check of 12 -ed/-ing words, a compound-sentence quiz, and an oral reading of the revised poem.

weeks.assessment: Compound-sentence quiz, spelling check, revised senses poem.

weeks.topic: Poetry recording and anthology
objectives: Create an audio recording of poems
Read poetry fluently with expression
Use new vocabulary to describe
materials: phone or tablet for audio recording

days.title: Gather poems
days.work: Choose 5 favorite poems from the unit (yours and published) for a personal anthology and copy them neatly.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice reading each poem at the right pace with expression; mark pauses with slashes. Phonics review game: two-syllable and compound-word bingo.

days.title: Record
days.work: Make an audio recording of 3 poems and listen back to self-assess pace and volume. Re-record one to improve it.

days.title: Illustrate
days.work: Add illustrations and a table of contents to the anthology. Write one sentence for each poem explaining why you chose it.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Poetry café: perform 2 poems for family. Unit test: identify rhyme, alliteration, and repetition in a new poem; spelling test of 15 unit words.

weeks.assessment: Poetry recording and anthology (rubric), unit test on poetic elements.

weeks.topic: Cinderella from France and China
objectives: Compare two versions of the same story
Use illustrations to understand setting
Read words with prefixes un-, re-, dis-
materials: Cinderella (Perrault, in Andrew Lang's The Blue Fairy Book, public domain)

days.title: Perrault's Cinderella
days.work: Read Perrault's Cinderella and list the story parts: kind girl, mean family, magic helper, event, lost item, happy ending. Phonics: prefix un- (unhappy, unlock).

days.title: Yeh-Shen
days.work: Read Yeh-Shen, a Cinderella story from China, and use the illustrations to describe the setting. Phonics: prefix re- (reread, retell, rebuild).

days.title: Compare
days.work: Fill a Venn diagram comparing Cinderella and Yeh-Shen (magic fish vs. fairy godmother, golden slipper vs. glass slipper). Phonics: prefix dis- (dislike, disagree).

days.title: Prefix meaning
days.work: Use prefixes to define 12 new words and use 4 in sentences. Discuss in a partner talk which magic helper is more interesting and why.

days.title: Week 21 review
days.work: Write 3 sentences: one way the stories are alike and two ways they are different. Spelling check of 12 prefix words.

weeks.assessment: Venn diagram and written compare/contrast sentences; prefix spelling check.

weeks.topic: Cinderella stories from Africa and North America
objectives: Compare and contrast multiple versions across cultures
Read words with suffixes -ful, -less, -ly, -er
State an opinion with a reason

days.title: Mufaro's Beautiful Daughters
days.work: Read Mufaro's Beautiful Daughters (Zimbabwe) and add it to a class comparison chart: main character, helper, test, ending. Phonics: suffixes -ful and -less (helpful, careless).

days.title: The Rough-Face Girl
days.work: Read The Rough-Face Girl (Algonquin) and add it to the chart; discuss what 'seeing' the Invisible Being means. Phonics: suffix -ly (kindly, quickly).

days.title: Adelita
days.work: Read Adelita (Mexico) and add it to the chart. Phonics: suffix -er (teacher, farmer, painter) and its meaning 'one who.'

days.title: Which is best
days.work: Discuss which Cinderella story is your favorite, giving reasons from the text, while practicing taking turns and building on each other's ideas. Write the opinion sentence and 2 reasons.

days.title: Week 22 review
days.work: Complete the comparison chart for 5 versions and write which two are most alike. Spelling check of 12 suffix words.

weeks.assessment: Completed comparison chart, opinion sentence with reasons, suffix spelling check.

weeks.topic: Point of view: whose story is it?
objectives: Acknowledge different characters' points of view
Read aloud in different voices
Draft an opinion piece with linking words
materials: The Three Little Pigs (any traditional version)
The True Story of the 3 Little Pigs! (Jon Scieszka)

days.title: Traditional pigs
days.work: Read The Three Little Pigs and retell it from the pigs' point of view. Practice voices for each pig and the wolf.

days.title: The wolf's side
days.work: Read The True Story of the 3 Little Pigs! and discuss how the wolf tells it differently. Chart what the pigs think vs. what the wolf claims.

days.title: Stepsister's view
days.work: Retell a scene from Cinderella in 4–5 sentences from a stepsister's point of view. Read it aloud in her voice.

days.title: Opinion draft
days.work: Draft the opinion piece 'The Best Cinderella Story' with an opening, opinion, 3 reasons using because, also, and another reason, and a concluding sentence.

days.title: Week 23 review
days.work: Read a short new fable and tell how two characters see the event differently. Peer/parent check of the opinion draft for linking words.

weeks.assessment: Point-of-view retelling and opinion draft with at least 3 linking words.

weeks.topic: Publishing opinions and comparatives
objectives: Revise and edit an opinion piece
Use comparative endings -er and -est
Present an opinion to an audience

days.title: Comparatives
days.work: Phonics/grammar: add -er and -est (tall, taller, tallest; happy, happier, happiest) and compare Cinderella characters ('Yeh-Shen's fish was kinder than…').

days.title: Revise the opinion
days.work: Strengthen reasons with examples from the books and add a closing that restates the opinion. Check that each reason starts with a linking word.

days.title: Edit and publish
days.work: Edit for capitals, end marks, and spelling of prefix/suffix words; publish as a poster with a book cover drawing.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the opinion poster to family and answer one question. Listen to a family member's opinion and ask a question about their reasons.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Unit test: compare two short versions of a folktale in a chart and sentences; decode 15 words with prefixes and suffixes; identify point of view.

weeks.assessment: Published opinion poster (opinion rubric) and unit test.

weeks.topic: Biography basics: Martin Luther King Jr.
objectives: Identify the main topic of a biography and paragraph focus
Describe connections between events in a life
Use reflexive pronouns
materials: A Picture Book of Martin Luther King, Jr. (David A. Adler)

days.title: What is a biography
days.work: Read A Picture Book of Martin Luther King, Jr. and learn that a biography tells about a real person's life in order. List 5 important events.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Put Dr. King's life events on a timeline strip and explain how one event led to the next (unfair laws → bus boycott → March on Washington).

days.title: Reflexive pronouns
days.work: Grammar: learn myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves, themselves; complete 10 sentences. Phonics: two-syllable words ending in -le (table, little, simple).

days.title: Paragraph focus
days.work: Reread 2 pages and write what each paragraph is mostly about. Discuss why Dr. King believed in peaceful protest.

days.title: Week 25 review
days.work: Answer 5 who/what/when/why/how questions on a ReadWorks biography passage. Spelling check of 10 -le words and a reflexive-pronoun quiz.

weeks.assessment: Timeline with cause/effect connections, comprehension questions, spelling and grammar quizzes.

weeks.topic: Biographies of courage: Rosa Parks and Jackie Robinson
objectives: Ask and answer questions about key details in biographies
Use apostrophes in contractions
Begin shared research
materials: I Am Rosa Parks and I Am Jackie Robinson (Brad Meltzer)

days.title: Rosa Parks
days.work: Read I Am Rosa Parks and discuss why her choice on the bus mattered. Answer how and why questions in complete sentences.

days.title: Jackie Robinson
days.work: Read I Am Jackie Robinson and compare the courage of Jackie and Rosa. Grammar: contractions with apostrophes (can't, didn't, he's, they're).

days.title: Choose a person
days.work: Choose a person who made a difference to research (e.g., Cesar Chavez, Sally Ride, Abraham Lincoln, Helen Keller, Marie Curie). Find 2 books or passages at the library.

days.title: Research questions
days.work: Write 3 research questions (When and where was this person born? What problem did they work on? How did they change things?). Start notes from the first source.

days.title: Week 26 review
days.work: Contractions quiz (12 items), read-aloud fluency check on a biography page, and research notes check.

weeks.assessment: Contractions quiz, fluency record, research question sheet and notes.

weeks.topic: Researching a person who made a difference
objectives: Gather information from sources to answer questions
Use possessive nouns with apostrophes
Capitalize names, holidays, and places
materials: Harvesting Hope: The Story of Cesar Chavez (Kathleen Krull)

days.title: Model biography
days.work: Read Harvesting Hope and notice how the author shows events in order and why Chavez's march mattered to farmworkers. Identify the author's purpose.

days.title: Second source
days.work: Take notes from a second source on your research person and add new facts to note cards (early life, challenge, actions, legacy).

days.title: Possessives
days.work: Grammar: singular possessives with 's (Rosa's bus, Cesar's march) and capitals for holidays, places, and names (Labor Day, Delano, California). Fix 10 sentences.

days.title: Organize notes
days.work: Sort note cards into 3 groups (early life, big work, why we remember them) and plan a paragraph for each.

days.title: Week 27 review
days.work: Draft the first paragraph of the biography report. Spelling check of 12 words with apostrophes and capitalized place names.

weeks.assessment: Organized note cards, first report paragraph, capitalization/possessive check.

weeks.topic: Writing and presenting a biography report
objectives: Write a 3-paragraph biography report
Use a visual display to clarify ideas
Recount information in an oral presentation

days.title: Draft paragraphs 2–3
days.work: Write the 'big work' and 'why we remember them' paragraphs with facts from notes and a concluding sentence.

days.title: Revise and edit
days.work: Revise for order and clarity; edit with checklist for capitals, apostrophes, and spelling. Make a final copy.

days.title: Visual display
days.work: Make a poster with a portrait, a 5-event timeline, and a quote or fact box to go with the report.

days.title: Living museum
days.work: Rehearse a 1-minute 'living museum' speech in first person as your research person ('I am Sally Ride…'), speaking audibly in complete sentences.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Present the living museum to family. Unit test: read a new short biography, sequence events, and identify the main topic and author's purpose.

weeks.assessment: Biography report and poster (research rubric), presentation, unit test.

weeks.topic: Volcanoes and earthquakes: reasons support points
objectives: Describe how reasons support an author's points
Use homophones correctly
Use diagrams to understand processes

days.title: Volcanoes
days.work: Read Volcanoes by Franklyn Branley and study the diagram of a volcano; label magma, crater, lava. Phonics: homophones to/two/too and there/their.

days.title: Author's points
days.work: Find the point 'Volcanoes can build new land' and list the reasons the author gives (Hawaii, Surtsey). Write: The author says ___ because ___.

days.title: Model eruption
days.work: Build a clay volcano and erupt it with baking soda and vinegar; write 3 steps of what happened. Phonics: homophone pairs (see/sea, right/write).

days.title: Earthquakes
days.work: Read a ReadWorks or library passage on earthquakes and identify one point and two reasons. Use context to define 'fault' and 'plates.'

days.title: Week 29 review
days.work: Reasons-and-points organizer on a new science passage; homophone quiz (12 items).

weeks.assessment: Point-and-reasons organizer, homophone quiz, written eruption steps.

weeks.topic: Comparing two texts on one topic
objectives: Compare the most important points of two texts on the same topic
Use a dictionary and alphabetical order
Write compound sentences
materials: How Mountains Are Made (Kathleen Weidner Zoehfeld)
second mountain text from ReadWorks or library

days.title: Text one
days.work: Read How Mountains Are Made and list 4 important points about how mountains form. Use the headings to locate facts.

days.title: Text two
days.work: Read a second text about mountains and list its important points. Mark points that are the same in both texts with a star.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Complete a two-text chart and write 3 compound sentences comparing the texts ('Both texts say…, but only the second…').

days.title: Dictionary skills
days.work: Alphabetize 10 science words to the second letter and use guide words to look them up in a children's dictionary; copy one definition for each.

days.title: Week 30 review
days.work: Compare two short passages on rocks in a chart, alphabetical order quiz, and a dictionary look-up check.

weeks.assessment: Two-text comparison chart and sentences; dictionary and ABC-order check.

weeks.topic: How-to writing: steps in a procedure
objectives: Describe connections between steps in a procedure
Write an informative how-to text
Read multisyllable words
materials: a seed-planting how-to from a seed packet

days.title: Read a procedure
days.work: Read the steps on a seed packet and a simple recipe; discuss why order matters and what happens if a step is skipped.

days.title: Follow the steps
days.work: Make trail mix following written steps, then rewrite the steps in your own words with numbers and time-order words. Phonics: multisyllable words (ingredient, measure).

days.title: Plan a how-to
days.work: Choose something you know how to do (make a sandwich, care for a pet, build a block tower) and list materials and steps.

days.title: Draft and test
days.work: Draft the how-to with an introduction, numbered steps, and a closing; have a family member follow it exactly and note any missing steps.

days.title: Week 31 review
days.work: Revise the how-to after the test, add diagrams, and publish. Spelling check of 12 multisyllable science words.

weeks.assessment: Published how-to text tested by a reader; spelling check.

weeks.topic: Friendly letters, formal and informal language
objectives: Write a friendly letter with commas in greeting and closing
Compare formal and informal English
Use precise science vocabulary

days.title: Formal vs. informal
days.work: Compare how you talk to a friend vs. how you would talk to a museum guide; rewrite 5 informal sentences in formal language.

days.title: Letter parts
days.work: Learn the 5 parts of a friendly letter (date, greeting, body, closing, signature) with commas in the greeting and closing; label a sample letter.

days.title: Write a letter
days.work: Write a letter to a relative explaining 3 things you learned about volcanoes, mountains, or earthquakes using science words.

days.title: Mail it
days.work: Edit the letter, address an envelope (capitalize city and state names), and mail it. Read a nonfiction passage independently and log it.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Unit test: cold read of two short science texts with questions comparing them and identifying the author's reasons; letter-format and comma check.

weeks.assessment: Friendly letter (format rubric) and unit test on comparing texts.

weeks.topic: Winnie-the-Pooh: following characters across chapters
objectives: Follow characters and plot across chapters of a chapter book
Read with expression in dialogue
Discuss books in a book club
materials: Winnie-the-Pooh (A. A. Milne, public domain in the U.S.)

days.title: Pooh and the bees
days.work: Read Chapter 1 of Winnie-the-Pooh (Pooh and the honey bees) and describe Pooh's plan and why it fails. Start a book-club journal page for the chapter.

days.title: Pooh gets stuck
days.work: Read Chapter 2 (Pooh visits Rabbit and gets stuck) and discuss how Pooh and Rabbit each respond to the problem. Read Pooh's dialogue in his voice.

days.title: Character traits
days.work: Make a character-trait web for Pooh, Piglet, Rabbit, Owl, and Eeyore with one example from the text for each.

days.title: Hunting the Woozle
days.work: Read Chapter 3 (Pooh and Piglet hunt a Woozle) and explain the joke. Book club: discuss with a family member, taking turns and asking questions.

days.title: Week 33 review
days.work: Answer written who/what/why questions on Chapters 1–3 and do a one-minute fluency read of a Pooh passage.

weeks.assessment: Book-club journal entries and written comprehension; fluency record.

weeks.topic: Winnie-the-Pooh: structure and points of view
objectives: Describe how chapters begin and end
Acknowledge different characters' points of view
Review irregular high-frequency words

days.title: Eeyore's tail
days.work: Read Chapter 4 (Eeyore loses a tail) and discuss how the beginning introduces the problem and the ending solves it.

days.title: Eeyore's birthday
days.work: Read Chapter 6 (Eeyore has a birthday) and tell the gift story from Piglet's point of view and then from Eeyore's.

days.title: Irregular word review
days.work: Review 30 irregularly spelled words (said, laugh, enough, friend, people, because) with a speed-read game and a spelling self-check.

days.title: Reader's theater
days.work: Perform a scene from Eeyore's birthday with different voices for Pooh, Piglet, and Eeyore.

days.title: Week 34 review
days.work: Story-structure chart for one chapter and a written paragraph explaining how two characters felt differently about the same event.

weeks.assessment: Story-structure chart and point-of-view paragraph; reader's theater performance.

weeks.topic: Book review: opinion writing about a favorite book
objectives: Write an opinion book review with reasons
Use digital tools to publish writing
Use vivid adjectives and adverbs

days.title: Finish Pooh
days.work: Read Chapter 10 (the party for Pooh) and discuss how the book ends. Rate Winnie-the-Pooh with stars and give one reason.

days.title: Plan a review
days.work: Choose the favorite book of the year and plan a review: summary without spoiling, opinion, 3 reasons, recommendation.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the book review using linking words and at least 4 strong describing words.

days.title: Type and publish
days.work: Type the review on a computer or tablet with help, add a picture of the cover, and print or share it.

days.title: Week 35 review
days.work: Read the review aloud and listen to a family member's review; spelling test of 20 review words from the year.

weeks.assessment: Published typed book review (opinion rubric) and cumulative spelling test.

weeks.topic: Year-end showcase and assessment
objectives: Show growth in reading, writing, and speaking
Reflect on goals as a reader and writer
Present a portfolio

days.title: End-of-year reading check
days.work: Read an on-level passage for a fluency check and answer comprehension questions; compare with the fall and mid-year scores.

days.title: Phonics inventory
days.work: Take the end-of-year phonics and spelling inventory (vowel teams, r-controlled, prefixes/suffixes, two-syllable words) and the reading of irregular words.

days.title: Portfolio selection
days.work: Choose 5 best pieces (narrative, fable, report, opinion, poem) and write a one-sentence reflection about each.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Present the portfolio to family, reading one favorite piece aloud and explaining one way you grew as a writer.

days.title: Summer reading plan
days.work: Make a summer reading list of 10 books (e.g., more Frog and Toad, Mercer Mayer, Magic Tree House) and set a reading goal. Celebrate the year.

weeks.assessment: End-of-year fluency and phonics inventory, portfolio presentation and reflections.
